research.summary: TE3 curriculum confirmed from the live ePerusteet API: 4 objectives (t1-t4) and 10 content areas (s1-s10, in groups of 3, 3 and 4). The YAML matches the API text. The TE3 module carries no extra guidance beyond its description; guidance (assessment, task, transversal competences) sits at subject level for Terveystieto (TE). TE1 and TE2 hold 20 topics (10 each, all briefed). They barely touch TE3 content: no topic covers disease epidemiology, services, self-care, ethics, prioritisation, or the historical and explanatory-model content. I propose 10 topics, TE3.01-TE3.10, serving every code in a teachable order.

findings.claim: The ePerusteet API for peruste 6828810 ('kaikki', about 4.28 MB JSON, HTTP 200) lists module TE3 id 6834849 'Terveys ja yhteiskunta' with 4 objectives (ids 9560256-9560259) and 3 content groups holding 3+3+4 = 10 items. This matches the required counts of 4 objectives and 10 contents.

data/curriculum-te1-te3.yaml agrees with the API: TE3.t1-t4 and TE3.s1-s10 with the same ids and wording (checked t1-t4 and s1-s10 against the parsed API). The file's source block lists peruste 6828810, diaarinumero OPH-2263-2019, valid from 2021-08-01, API modified 2026-04-14, checked 2026-11-21. TE3 is 2 credits and not compulsory.

The TE3 module object has only the keys id, nimi, pakollinen, koodi, laajuus, kuvaus, tavoitteet, sisallot and a few reference fields. It has no module-level guidance text such as assessment or teaching notes. Extra guidance exists only at subject level (Terveystieto, id 6834386): task (tehtava), assessment (arviointi), transversal competences (laajaAlaisetOsaamiset). Those fields were read: assessment targets facts and concepts, information skills, applying and analysing, justifying, and examining ethical questions. Assessment does not target the student's own values, attitudes or health behaviour. Brief 010's rule of no personal disclosure follows this. The module description names three focuses: historical lines and future challenges, non-communicable and infectious disease plus services, self-care and own care, and ethics plus global health challenges.

WebFetch of the API URL could read only the first 100000 of 4.2 million characters, so the check was done with curl and a local JSON parse. Brief writers should use the fetcher or curl, not WebFetch, for this endpoint.

Existing topics (front matter module, title, curriculum): TE1 has 10 topics: 01 Mitä terveys on [t1,s1], 02 Elintapamallit [t2,s2], 03 Terveyskulttuuri [t2,s3: medikalisaatio, vaihtoehtohoidot], 04 Ravinto [s4], 05 Liikunta ja uni [s4], 06 Seksuaaliterveys [s5], 07 Seksuaalioikeudet [s5], 08 Mielenterveys [s6], 09 Stressi ja kriisit [s6], 10 Opiskeluhyvinvointi [s7]. TE2 has 10 topics: 01 Tieto ja vinoumat, 02 Tutkimustieto, 03 Terveysviestintä, 04 Elinympäristö (radon and lung cancer; eriarvoisuus defined), 05 Psykososiaalinen ympäristö, 06 Kestävä kehitys (Terveys kaikissa politiikoissa defined with an exam task), 07 Turvallisuus ja väkivalta, 08 Työhyvinvointi, 09 Riippuvuuden mekanismit, 10 Riippuvuudet (tobacco: COPD, lung cancer, CVD; alcohol and cancer; carcinogen classes).

Keyword search of content/topics shows no coverage yet of: itsehoito, priorisoi, hedelmöity, abortti, eutanasia, Pohjois-Karjala, diabetes, 'selitysmall'. 'Epidemiolog' appears only in a Yle link title. Infectious disease appears only as a global-factor list item (TE1.01), the vaccination effect on antibodies in a sleep topic (TE2.05), and the STI notification classes in TE1.06, which says the topic is deepened in TE3 (so TE3.04 must link back and not repeat). 'Seulont' and 'geeni' are incidental. 'hyve' and 'eettinen' appear in passing in many topics but no topic teaches ethical analysis.

Per-code overlap with TE1 and TE2. s1: partly TE1.03 (medikalisaatio, uskomushoidot, health culture) and TE1.01 (WHO definition); new are historical health concepts (biomedical, biopsychosocial, salutogenic, lay vs scientific) and explanatory models of disease (miasma, germ theory, risk factor, multifactorial). s2: TE1.01 gives the determinants and the Health-in-All-Policies idea sits in TE2.06; new are the history of population health (hygiene, sanitation, vaccination, antibiotics, screening, the North Karelia project, welfare state, THL/neuvola/school health history) and the policy history of Health in All Policies (link, do not redefine). s3: TE2.06 (sustainability) and TE2.03 (communication) are adjacent; new are AMR, ageing, climate and pandemics, digitalisation, genomics and AI in health, inequality and mental health as challenges. s4: TE1.04-05 (nutrition, activity, sleep) and TE2.10 (tobacco, alcohol harms) supply risk factors; new are the epidemiological transition, incidence and prevalence, the main diseases, infectious-disease transmission, prevention levels, vaccines, antibiotic resistance. s5: TE1.01 and TE1.10 name student health care; new are the whole service system (wellbeing services counties, public/private/third sector, Kela, who to go to). s6: TE1 and TE2 have no coverage; new are the concepts and limits of self-care and own care, medicines and reliable sources. s7: no existing coverage; new are the ethical frameworks. s8: TE1.07 touches rights and consent, TE1.06 covers contraception and STI; all of fertility treatment, abortion, screening, gene technology, euthanasia and lifestyle freedom are new. s9: new (ethical principles, patients' rights, prioritisation). s10: TE1.01 and TE2.04 define eriarvoisuus in one line; new are figure-reading of inequality in Finland, global health (WHO, SDGs) and ways to narrow gaps. TE3.t2 builds on TE2.10 and TE2.01 (risk and evidence).

The existing topics' own wording shows a convention to follow: TE1.06 states that STI classification is 'deepened in TE3', and every earlier topic ends with the exam-task note that the rest comes from TE3. TE3 should therefore keep the 'Tehtävät' footer format (fictional material, exam task types, model answers).

The proposed topic list is below. Order matters: history and concepts first, then disease, services and self-care, then the ethics framework used by three later topics, then inequality as the closing synthesis. Codes per topic: (01) Terveyskäsitykset ja sairauksien selitysmallit: s1, t1. (02) Miten yhteiskunta, tiede ja teknologia ovat muuttaneet väestön terveyttä (epidemiological transition as introduction, North Karelia, welfare state, Health in All Policies as history, vaccines, sanitation): s2, s4 (transition part), t1. (03) Tarttumattomat sairaudet: riskitekijät ja ehkäisy (CVD, type 2 diabetes, cancers, COPD, memory disorders; incidence vs prevalence; prevention levels; no blaming): s4, t2. (04) Tartuntataudit, rokotukset ja mikrobilääkeresistenssi (transmission routes, herd immunity, waterborne and tick-borne, STI link to TE1.06, AMR): s4, t2. (05) Sosiaali- ja terveyspalvelut: järjestäminen, tuottaminen ja käyttäminen (hyvinvointialueet, public/private/third sector, Kela, who to go to in which situation, critique): s5, t3. (06) Itsehoito, omahoito ja lääkkeet (self-care vs own care, long-term illness, medicines, Fimea, when to seek care; no medical advice): s6, t3, t2 (consequences for individual). (07) Eettisen analysoinnin näkökulmat (virtues, consequences, rights, duties, motives, values, norms as an exam-ready framework with cases): s7, t4. (08) Eettiset ja oikeudelliset kysymykset: hedelmöityshoidot, abortti, seulonnat, geeniteknologia (balanced, inclusive, laws and positions): s8 (part), t4. (09) Elämän loppu, elintapojen vapaus ja vastuu, potilaan oikeudet ja priorisointi (euthanasia with safe messaging, lifestyle freedom and responsibility, health-care ethical principles, patients' rights, prioritisation): s8 (part), s9, t4, t3 (critique). (10) Terveyden eriarvoisuus Suomessa ja maailmalla sekä tulevaisuuden haasteet (figure reading, narrowing gaps, global health, future challenges): s10, s3, t4, t1. Option: split 09 into an end-of-life and lifestyle topic and a patients-rights and prioritisation topic, with s3 moving to 02 plus 10, to reach 11 topics, if the writers hit the 460-line cap.

Coverage check for the proposal: s1->01; s2->02; s3->10 and 02; s4->02,03,04; s5->05; s6->06; s7->07; s8->08 and 09; s9->09; s10->10. t1->01,02,10; t2->03,04,06; t3->05,06,09; t4->07,08,09,10. All 10 contents and 4 objectives are served, and t2 and t4 each have three or more topics.

recommendations: Use the 10-topic order above; it reaches every TE3 code and puts ethical frameworks (07) before the three topics that use them (08, 09, 10).
Fetch curriculum with curl or the site's own fetcher: WebFetch cannot read the 4.2 MB API response.
Do not redefine Health in All Policies, eriarvoisuus, medikalisaatio or the STI classes: link to TE2.06, TE2.04, TE1.03 and TE1.06, and put the new angle (history, figures, ethics) in TE3.
Add the TE2.10 tobacco and alcohol cancer and COPD facts as links from TE3.03 rather than copying, and cross-link radon from TE2.04.

Assessment guidance says grade analysis and justification, not students' own values or behaviour; keep every TE3 ethics task on fictional cases and avoid asking for personal positions or health data (consistent with brief 010 and CLAUDE.md).
Topics 03, 04, 08 and 09 carry the most facts; plan for the 460-line cap there and split 09 if needed.
research.versus_expected: The brief's expected answer is confirmed on the counts (4 objectives, 10 contents) and the three content groups. The brief's ten expected topics map almost one to one onto my list. Differences: the brief lists 'future health challenges' with inequality and the epidemiological transition with history; I place s3 (future challenges) in topic 10 with inequality and in 02, and I put the transition's concepts in 02 and the disease detail in 03 and 04. I also merge lifestyle freedom, euthanasia, patients' rights and prioritisation into topic 09 (the brief had euthanasia in the ethical-questions topic and rights and prioritisation separate), because that gives balanced topic sizes; a split is the stated fallback. New finding not in the brief: ePerusteet gives no module-level guidance beyond the module description, so subject-level assessment text is the only extra guidance. Another new finding: existing TE1 and TE2 topics already define Health in All Policies, eriarvoisuus and STI classes, so TE3 should link to them. A third: itsehoito, priorisointi, abortti, eutanasia and fertility treatment are entirely new.

research.summary: I opened about 70 pages on 2026-11-21 and recorded 4 to 6 candidates for most TE3 areas, with thin coverage for three of them (see 'Gaps'). Almost everything is link-out. No page I read carried an open licence (CC BY or CC BY-SA). Terveyskirjasto, Sydänliitto, Kela, OPH, MLL and Yle show only a copyright notice or "all rights reserved". THL, STM, Finlex, WHO, Fimea, ETENE, Palko and Käypä hoito state no licence on the pages I read. The one licence line I read in full was Sydänliitto's: all rights reserved. I did not open THL's, Finlex's or WHO's licence terms pages, so a licence may be stated there. I found no open CC BY lukio TE3 material, so the expected answer that almost all links would be link-out holds. I classed unlicensed pages as link-out. Finlex statutes may be freely quotable, but no page I read says so, so that is unverified. Per-claim 'access' fields use the form open|link-out|excluded plus the licence note. Format of each finding below: [area] Title | publisher | URL | licence class | audience as the page states it | read 2026-11-21 | date shown.

research.summary: Facts-laws aspect for TE3. Read directly: Finlex open data API (XML for 785/1992, 239/1970, 1237/2006; all read 2026-11-21, consolidated texts dated 2023-04-14 and 2025-06-27), STM, Kela, THL (English vaccination page), Terveyskirjasto, valtioneuvosto.fi. Finlex's web pages and eduskunta.fi, etene.fi tasks, thl.fi Finnish vaccination pages, Cancer Registry were not readable. Stable rules can be stated in original words (patient self-determination, 12-week abortion rule, fertility treatment conditions, presumed consent in organ donation, hoitotahto binding effect, euthanasia not permitted); every figure, age, fee, date and pending bill must stay a link. Two live items to watch: the euthanasia citizens' initiative KAA 4/2024 is still in committee (as of 5.10.2026 press), and a government proposal to put palliative and end-of-life care explicitly in the Health Care Act (target 1.1.2027) was out for comment in spring 2026.

findings.claim: Patients' rights act is Laki potilaan asemasta ja oikeuksista 785/1992; Finlex consolidated version dated 2023-04-14 (produced 2026-10-15). Stable rule: patient is treated in agreement with them (6 §); if patient refuses a treatment, other medically acceptable care is sought together; urgent care is given to avert danger to life, but a firmly and validly stated earlier wish is respected (8 §); minors who can decide by age and development may forbid disclosure of their health information to guardians (9 §); dissatisfied patient may file a muistutus (10 §).

Abortion act (Laki raskauden keskeyttämisestä 239/1970): since the 1.9.2023 reform a pregnancy can be ended on the pregnant person's own request to the end of week 12; later terminations need a permit (week 20 limit, 24 for severe fetal disease per 5 and 5a §); the reform added a right to psychosocial support; private providers need no separate permit for early terminations. Source for reform is STM release 111/2023 dated 2023-09-01. NOTE: the Finlex consolidated text (dated 2025-06-27) still reads in the older wording (grounds list, two-doctor decision), so Finlex text and STM release must be checked together before writing grounds.

Recent change: amending act 762/2025 (published 11.7.2025, in force 1.1.2026) amends the abortion act (sections 1, 5, 5a, 6, 10, 11, 15; repeals 10a) and moves handling of abortion and sterilisation matters from Valvira to a board at Lupa- ja valvontavirasto. Read from the act's Finlex PDF via search snippet, and the amendment list in the Finlex XML; the exact practical content for patients was not read.

Fertility treatment act is Laki hedelmöityshoidoista 1237/2006 (Finlex consolidated 2025-06-27; latest amending act listed 547/2025). Stable rules read in text: treatment needs the recipient's written consent (8 §); not given if the couple's partner is married to someone else, if pregnancy would endanger health, if the child's balanced development cannot be assured, or if adoption is intended; gamete donors must be 18 or over and health-checked (13 §); donors are identified by a code (14 §); a person who may have been born from donation may at 18 get the donor code and, by notifying the donor register, the donor identity (23 §); selecting traits is allowed only for serious disease or sex linked to serious disease (5 §).
Content of 547/2025 amendment to the fertility act and any pending fertility-law reform (surrogacy, donor anonymity, treatment of single people) was not read.

National vaccination programme: STM decides content, wellbeing services counties organise delivery, THL gives guidelines and monitors; programme vaccines are voluntary and free of charge, state-funded. THL page has three tables (children/adolescents about 2 months to 14-15 years, adults at 25/pregnancy, 45, 65, over 65, and risk groups). THL page last updated 9.10.2026 per page. dTaP in pregnancy part of programme from 1.7.2025 (search snippet of THL professional page). Adult varicella vaccination started 2026 (THL release seen via snippet only). Age schedule and vaccine list change, so link only.

Wellbeing services counties: 21 counties took over organising social and health services and rescue services at the start of 2023; Helsinki is not in a county and organises its own services; HUS handles some specialised tasks. STM page shows no own date; newest news item on it 17.8.2026.

Student health care: organised by the wellbeing services county where the school is located; free of charge for students under 18; upper secondary students covered (STM English page, no update date shown). Search snippets of THL/STM say adults' sickness care in student health care may carry client fees, upper secondary students can see the public health nurse without appointment, and from autumn 2026 all upper secondary students fill an electronic health survey (Omaolo) with a health check by the year they turn 18; these were not read on the page.

Client fees: 2026 annual fee ceiling for public health care is 815 euros, indexed every second year; fees for a person under 18 are added to the guardian's fees toward the ceiling (STM page, no own date; newest item 21.9.2026). STM fee page 'Terveydenhuollon maksut 2026' and a 2026 index table exist; search snippet says a government proposal on fee changes was submitted 21.9.2026 to take effect 1.3.2027 (details not read). All amounts must stay links.

Kela medicine reimbursement: three classes (basic 40%, lower special 65%, upper special 100% with 4.50 euro co-payment per purchase); 2026 initial deductible 70.33 euros (Kela apteekkitiedote 11/2025, 15.10.2025) and annual cap 636.12 euros; 2027 annual cap 650.56 euros stated in news item on the Kela medicines page, page updated 10.11.2026. The initial deductible does not apply to children and young people and applies from the start of the year of turning 19 (search snippet, not read on page). All figures change yearly, so link only.

Medicines rules (Fimea): Fimea assigns each product and pack size a prescription or self-care status; self-care packs carry the label 'Itsehoitolääke'; some self-care medicines require extra counselling at the pharmacy and are marked in a Fimea list. Only the extra-counselling page was read (no date shown); the rest comes from search results of fimea.fi. The exact legal criteria (Medicines Act, Medicines Decree) were not read.

Screening programmes: search result summaries of STM and Cancer Registry pages give breast cancer (women 50-69, about every two years), cervical (30-65, every five years, HPV test, papa under 30 per THL material) and colorectal (rolling out from 2022 by birth cohort, full 56-74 target group in 2031). None of these pages could be read, and sources conflict on cervical ages, so ages and intervals must be linked, not typed. THL material read via snippet says Finnish cervical screening is free and effective and that the programme HPV vaccine protects against about 9 in 10 cervical cancers.

ETENE (Valtakunnallinen sosiaali- ja terveysalan eettinen neuvottelukunta) is an advisory board whose site lists statements, position papers and published ethical principles (also in Swedish and English); established 1998 by decree, task wording is 'to discuss ethical questions of social and health care and patient/client position' (from secondary-source snippets quoting etene.fi). Appointer and tasks section not readable on the page; ETENE gave a 2026 statement on the palliative care draft.

Organ donation: since the law change on 1.8.2010 organ removal after death may go ahead unless the deceased is known or presumed to have opposed it in life; relatives have no right to forbid but are heard when the wish is unknown; a minor who could not form a view needs guardian consent; the wish can be oral or written. Rule read in STM release dated 24.8.2010 and confirmed by search summary; the statute is Laki ihmisen elimien, kudoksien ja solujen lääketieteellisestä käytöstä 101/2001 (title verified on Finlex, text not read; death definition and DCDD details from snippet only). Current stm.fi/elinluovutus page gave 404.

Hoitotahto (living will): voluntary; applies only when the person cannot decide about care; a refusal of a specific treatment binds professionals and relatives cannot change it; other wishes are not binding but followed where possible; recommended store is Omakanta (Kanta), paper needs own signature and date, oral wish can be recorded in the record; only the maker can change it. Terveyskirjasto article dlk00809, Kustannus Oy Duodecim, updated 22.6.2026. The statutory anchor is 785/1992 6 § (earlier expressed wish) and 8 § (firmly and validly stated wish prevails in urgent care), both read in the act.

Euthanasia is not permitted under Finnish law (STM statement via search result; no Finlex provision read that allows it). The 2017 citizens' initiative KAA 2/2017 was rejected by Parliament in plenary on 4.5.2018 (Verkkouutiset same day; Heinonen counter-proposal lost 128-60); parliament asked for a palliative-care working group. The 2024 initiative 'Eutanasialaki säädettävä Suomeen' (KAA 4/2024) was handed in 29.5.2024 with 53,483 statements, sent to the Social Affairs and Health Committee 5.9.2024, committee hearing 11.6.2025; per MTV Uutiset 5.10.2026 the committee had still not finished it and the initiative lapses if not handled in this electoral term. ECHR ruled 18.6.2024 that an ALS patient had no right to assisted death (Edilex listing).

Pending proposal related to end of life: STM draft government proposal (consultation 24.2 to 7.4.2026; STM release 25.2.2026) to state in the Health Care Act that palliative care and end-of-life care are the wellbeing services county's responsibility and define them; also change of health centre every three months instead of yearly and monthly waiting-time reporting. Entry into force 1.1.2027 appears in search summaries but not on the release page. Final government bill not found.

Finlex open data API works with plain curl: https://opendata.finlex.fi/finlex/avoindata/v1/akn/fi/act/statute-consolidated/{year}/{number} returns consolidated AKN XML (UTF-8; decode as UTF-8, not cp1252) with FRBR dateConsolidated and dateProduced fields. The Finlex human pages (finlex.fi/fi/lainsaadanto/...) return only navigation to WebFetch because they are JavaScript-rendered, so link to them for readers but read via the API.

recommendations: Link, never type: client fee amounts and the fee ceiling, Kela deductibles and the cap (change yearly), vaccination table ages and vaccines, screening target ages and intervals, abortion week limits as a figure for exam use (state the principle, link the law), number of wellbeing services counties, any pending bill (palliative care, fee changes from 1.3.2027, the euthanasia initiative).

Stable rules safe in original words: the patient is treated in agreement with them and may refuse a treatment; urgent care is given to avert danger but a clearly expressed earlier wish is respected; a hoitotahto binds only for refusals of named treatments and only when the person cannot decide; organ donation after death rests on presumed consent with a lifelong right to object; euthanasia is not permitted and Parliament has so far not changed that; student health care is organised by the wellbeing services county and free to under 18s; programme vaccines are voluntary and free.

Abortion topic: use STM release 111/2023 plus Finlex 239/1970 and note that Finlex text still carries old grounds wording while the 2023 reform and 762/2025 (1.1.2026, authority moved to Lupa- ja valvontavirasto) are in force; have a human reviewer check the combined reading before publishing. Present legal facts and the main ethical positions without moralising.

Euthanasia topic: describe the legal status and the existence of citizens' initiatives, the ECHR 2024 ruling and the palliative care bill as links dated with the read date; no methods; add a help box; state that the initiative status was last seen on 5.10.2026 and may have changed.

research.summary: Epidemiology aspect for TE3: concept definitions have official Finnish sources (Terveyskirjasto/Duodecim for incidence and prevalence; WHO for herd immunity and NCD risk factors; Tilastokeskus for mortality and life expectancy). Live-figure locations were verified for TBE, Lyme, waterborne outbreaks, STIs, cancer, antibiotic resistance and respiratory viruses; pages should link to these and never type the numbers. Several guessed THL URLs returned 404, and the Syöpärekisteri Finnish site returned 403. The English cancerregistry.fi page was read instead. DALY, epidemiological transition, COPD, memory disorders and Finnish NCD burden were not verified from a primary page.

findings.claim: Ilmaantuvuus (incidence) = new cases in a population over a period, usually per person-years; distinct from esiintyvyys/vallitsevuus (prevalence = share of cases in a population at a time or period). Terveyskirjasto medical glossary, dated 18.10.2016. No licence stated (copyright Duodecim): link-out only.
Terveyskirjasto has a companion glossary entry for vallitsevuus (prevalence). Seen only in search results, page not opened.

WHO defines herd immunity as indirect protection when enough of a population is immune through vaccination or earlier infection. WHO says to reach it through vaccination, not by letting disease spread. It cites about 95% for measles and about 80% for polio. Page dated 31 Dec 2020 and no longer updated, so cite it for the concept only.

WHO NCD fact sheet (updated 25 Sep 2025) names four main NCD groups: cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes. Modifiable behavioural risks: tobacco, unhealthy diet, harmful alcohol use, insufficient physical activity. Metabolic risks: raised blood pressure, overweight/obesity, high blood glucose, abnormal lipids. It does not list memory or mental disorders as main groups.

Tilastokeskus 'Kuolleet' statistic (updated 24 Apr 2026) holds deaths, infant mortality and life expectancy at birth by sex, 1990-2025, with detail in StatFin. Causes of death are a separate statistic, 'Kuolemansyyt'. Link the statistic instead of typing the figure.

TBE: laboratories report cases to THL's tartuntatautirekisteri. THL runs an interactive municipality-level map of incidence and vaccination areas (raportointi.thl.fi). Vaccination areas are set from a five-year rolling average, with about 15 per 100,000 as the usual threshold. The page itself shows no date.

TBE vaccine page (updated 2 Jul 2026): ticks spread TBE, and unpasteurised milk can too. The free programme vaccine is for people aged 3+ living in listed risk areas, and the list changes yearly. The vaccine does not protect against Lyme borreliosis, which has no vaccine, and does not stop tick bites. Boosters are outside the programme.

Lyme borreliosis case counts are in THL's tartuntatautirekisteri statistics database (sampo.thl.fi). Borrelia findings are notifiable microbe findings. The year count has risen since 1995. Seen via search summary only (not opened), so no figures should be copied.

THL food- and waterborne infections page (updated 30 Sep 2026): suspected outbreaks go to the RYMY register (THL and Ruokavirasto). Norovirus is about a third of outbreaks over 2010-2024 and the cause is unknown in about 36%. Household and bathing-water outbreak counts are listed by year. The page links Ruokavirasto open data and the infectious disease register database.

Most Finnish waterborne outbreaks are caused by norovirus and Campylobacter, usually from contaminated groundwater or small supplies after surface or wastewater gets in. Seen only in a search summary of THL pages. The THL waterborne-outbreaks page and the water-treatment details (disinfection, UV, chlorination) were not read.

STIs: THL sexual and reproductive health statistics page (updated 5 Nov 2026) lists 2025 chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis case figures and links to the STI and chronic viral hepatitis statistics page. A page citing these should link them, not copy them. Chlamydia is reported by laboratories, not by physician notification.

Measles: THL says herd immunity needs about 95% immune. Two MMR doses are given, at 12 months and 6 years, and are free. THL has noted a fall in second-dose coverage. Protection can be incomplete in people born 1965-1975 and in some born abroad. Seen via search summary of THL pages only.

Syöpärekisteri English statistics page: interactive cancer statistics application (incidence, mortality, survival), screening statistics application, thematic statistics, annual report 'Cancer in Finland 2024', and links to NORDCAN, NordScreen and Globocan. Prevalence is not mentioned. No licence or reuse terms stated. The Finnish site returned 403.

Antibiotic resistance: THL coordinates the FiRe network of 21 clinical microbiology laboratories. The public Finres cube on sampo.thl.fi holds susceptibility results. Ruokavirasto publishes Finres-Vet for animals. Search results only, not opened.

Influenza and COVID-19: THL publishes autumn 2026 COVID vaccination recommendations, flu vaccine advice and wastewater monitoring of influenza, RSV and SARS-CoV-2. Seen in search snippets, no page opened. Link the current THL influenza and coronavirus pages and copy no season figures.

Käypä hoito (Duodecim) is independent evidence-based national clinical guidance with plain-language patient versions. No licence name is visible and copyright is held by Duodecim, so treat it as link-out. Professionals are the main audience, so pages should point students to the patient versions.

Finnish NCD burden context (type 2 diabetes incidence and prevalence trends, coronary disease as the most common cardiovascular disease, regional differences) appeared only in secondary sources (news and a core.ac.uk THL brief). COPD and memory disorder prevalence figures were not found. These should not be asserted until a THL, Käypä hoito or Muistiliitto page is read.

DALY, epidemiological transition, mortality vs morbidity, zoonosis and pandemic: no primary page was read. WHO indicator registry page 158 only returned navigation, so DALY is not defined by a read source.

recommendations: Link, never type, any case count, incidence or life expectancy: use THL's tartuntatautirekisteri database (sampo.thl.fi), the THL TBE map, THL's food- and waterborne infections page, THL's sexual health statistics page, Syöpärekisteri's interactive application, Tilastokeskus StatFin and the WHO NCD fact sheet. Give each link the date it was read.

Concept glossary: use Terveyskirjasto for ilmaantuvuus and vallitsevuus and WHO for herd immunity and NCD risk factors, and write the rest (mortality, morbidity, epidemic, pandemic, zoonosis, epidemiological transition) in original words. Read one primary page each for DALY (WHO or IHME GBD), epidemiological transition and zoonosis (THL or Ruokavirasto) first, or label them model-only.

Read still-missing primary pages before the content workflow: THL waterborne-outbreaks page and water treatment (also STUK/Valvira or Ruokavirasto drinking-water pages), a THL page on Lyme disease, THL COPD and memory-disorder pages or Muistiliitto, THL Kansantaudit or the FinTerveys report, and WHO or THL pages on antibiotic resistance and zoonoses.

Chart tasks should use fictional numbers invented for the task. State that the data are made up and teach reading the axes, incidence vs prevalence, rate vs count and a population denominator, for example a made-up TBE or chlamydia rate by age band. Do not reuse register figures as the dataset, since they change.

Disease pages: describe risk factors as population-level and shaped by environment, income and access, with no language that blames individuals. Say that cancer, COPD, diabetes and memory disorders also occur in people with no risk factors. Point to student health care or a doctor for one's own symptoms. Keep the vaccine content evidence-based without false balance, and state that TBE vaccine does not cover Lyme.

Licence class: Terveyskirjasto, Käypä hoito, Syöpärekisteri and THL pages show no open licence on the pages read, so treat all as link-out. Re-check THL's reuse terms only if text is to be adapted. WHO terms were not read.
For waterborne and tick-borne exam content, link THL's RYMY-based page and the TBE map instead of copying lists of risk areas, since the area list changes yearly (as of the January 2026 expansion).
research.versus_expected: The brief's expectation of THL, Terveyskirjasto, Käypä hoito and WHO as mostly link-out sources holds: no open licence was found on any page read. The expected disease coverage (cardiovascular, T2D, cancers, COPD, memory) is only partly supported. WHO names cardiovascular, cancer, chronic respiratory disease and diabetes, but memory and mental disorders and Finnish prevalence figures lack a verified primary page. Infectious disease sources (TBE, waterborne, STI, measles, antibiotic resistance, respiratory viruses) are well covered by THL pages that can be linked. Several guessed THL URLs returned 404 and many THL pages were seen only as search summaries, so more page reads are needed than the brief assumed.

research.summary: Partial primary reads. Confirmed: ETENE's role and positions (page limited), Sekasin serves ages 12-29 (own page), Mieli Kriisipuhelin 09 2525 0111 is 24h but is a general adult-and-youth service, not youth-specific, and the 2018-2021 euthanasia working group result. Finlex act pages (abortion, patients' rights) returned only navigation, so legal specifics are unverified. THL vaccine page, Mieli suicide page and Duodecim etiikka were not readable. Concrete writer and checker rules below rest partly on model knowledge and are graded accordingly.

findings.claim: ETENE is the National Advisory Board on Social Welfare and Health Care Ethics; its English site lists statements (e.g. intersex children 2016, experimental care 2016) and sections 'Duties and members', 'Statements and opinions', 'Publications'. The fetched page gave no end-of-life or principles text, so link the statements and publications pages and read them before citing positions.

Sekasin chat: anonymous, free, for ages 12-29; open daily (weekdays 9-24, weekends 15-24 per page read today); under-16s are pointed to Apuu-chat. Qualifies as a youth help link; hours are changing facts, so link not copy.

MIELI ry Kriisipuhelin 09 2525 0111 is open 24h, anonymous, Finnish only; the page does not say it is youth-specific (it serves people in crisis generally), though Mieli lists peer groups for young people and support for suicidal thoughts. Under the brief's rule (help links only to services whose own pages say they serve young people), use Sekasin as the youth link and Mieli as a general 24h line with that wording, or link only the youth peer-group page after reading it.

Euthanasia in Finland: expert working group (8.5.2018-30.6.2021, report 31.8.2021) was unanimous that palliative and terminal care need developing, proposed amending the Patients' Rights Act, Health Care Act and Health Insurance Act, and did NOT reach a shared view on legalising euthanasia or assisted suicide; it drafted two possible laws and noted a third option of keeping current law. Good balanced anchor: present as 'no shared view' and 'open question', with date.

Search snippets say active euthanasia is prosecutable as homicide under the Criminal Code while forgoing futile treatment (passive form) is accepted; Finnish Medical Association opposes active euthanasia. Only secondary or snippet sources read; confirm on Finlex (Rikoslaki) and the Lääkäriliitto 2024 background document before stating.

Finlex pages for the Abortion Act 239/1970 and Patients' Rights Act 785/1992 exist and are current consolidated texts, but the fetch returned only navigation, so grounds, week limits, age rules, hoitotahto and sections 6 and 8 are NOT verified here. A fact-checker must read the Finlex text or the THL/STM page on abortion before the week and grounds are written.

Ethical-analysis viewpoints, kid-friendly framing from a Finnish lukio health-education handout (Ahola-Launonen, 2018): consequentialism asks how welfare is maximised and harm minimised; rights and duty ethics ask what rights and duties exist; virtue ethics asks what a morally ideal person would do (Aristotelian tradition). A lukio philosophy glossary matches. Tieteen termipankki search did not return definitions for these terms, so do not cite it for them without a direct hit.

WHO media guidance for suicide reporting (2023 update) stresses stories of coping and recovery, hope, and online/social-media considerations; the specific do/don't list was not on the fetched page (in a PDF). Use as the named safe-messaging basis; checker must open the PDF in WHO IRIS to cite items.
Duodecim Terveyskirjasto is dated and authored (example page 31.3.2025) and is suitable as a dated link target; the page tested had no ethics content, so Duodecim etiikka as a source was not located.

recommendations: RULES FOR ALL ETHICS PAGES: (1) Legal facts first, in a box headed 'Mitä laki sanoo', each with Finlex or THL/STM link and date read; (2) then 'Eri näkökulmia': at least two or three positions labelled as positions, each stated in the words its holders would use, with the same length and tone, applied through the viewpoints (consequences, rights, duties, virtues, motives, values, norms); (3) the page never gives the answer and tasks ask students to analyse, not to say which side is right; (4) separate 'is' from 'ought': legal status, medical facts and values never share a sentence; (5) no loaded terms (not 'murha', 'tappaa lapsen', 'designer baby', 'kuolemanapu' as euphemism); use the statutory or clinical term and define it once; (6) no first-person or hypothetical about the student's own life; no task asks 'what would you do', use third-person cases or invented fictional persons (no real named individuals); (7) say 'many people, including believers and non-believers, hold differing views' rather than assigning views to groups; (8) inclusive: fertility treatment text covers single people, same-sex couples and trans people only as the current law allows (verify the Hedelmöityshoitolaki 2006 and its 2023 changes on Finlex before writing), without implying a 'normal' family; abortion text avoids judging reasons or women; use 'raskaana oleva' where the law's group is wider than women.

CHECKER TESTS (pass/fail): does each ethical page contain a legal-facts block with dated links; at least two distinct positions with symmetric treatment; no sentence that tells the student what to conclude; no emotive vocabulary; no method, dose, route or tool for ending life; help box present on end-of-life page; no real person or case named; every legal figure (weeks, ages) matches the Finlex text read in the same session; every viewpoint (virtue, consequence, rights, duty, motive, value, norm) defined once in own words with a neutral example not drawn from the sensitive topics.

EUTHANASIA/END-OF-LIFE: teach distinctions (palliative care, terminal care, forgoing treatment, hoitotahto, euthanasia, assisted suicide) as definitions with legal status; anchor the debate in the 2021 working group's 'no shared view' and Parliament's handling of the citizens' initiative (read the eduskunta page before citing); never describe how, with what, or where; no case stories of suicide; no numbers on methods; present palliative care as available and a right to symptom relief (verify the Patients' Rights Act wording); help box always: Sekasin (12-29, own page), Mieli Kriisipuhelin as general 24h line, plus 112 for emergencies and opiskeluterveydenhuolto; add a content note 'Aihe voi herättää tunteita, esimerkiksi läheisen kuolema tai omat ajatukset' and a line that the student can leave the page or talk to a trusted adult.

SAFETY FLAGS (contract set): euthanasia or end-of-life page = suicide_selfharm (help box mandatory) plus content note; abortion, fertility treatment, STIs, screening in pregnancy, gene technology about reproduction = sexuality; no flag for gene technology generally, prioritisation, patients' rights or vaccines; eating, substances and violence only if the NCD or lifestyle topic mentions them: alcohol/tobacco as risk factors are factual and low-risk but flag substances if the page describes use patterns, and cancer-risk pages that mention diet need no eating flag unless weight, calories or dieting appear (which the rules ban anyway). Content note (not flag) for cancer, memory disorders, grief, miscarriage, infertility, prenatal-screening results, and chronic illness, because students may have personal experience.

AVOID BLAME IN DISEASE CONTENT: describe risk factors as population-level probabilities, not causes in an individual; say 'riskitekijä' not 'syy'; always add structural and genetic factors (income, work, environment, heredity) beside lifestyle; no 'omaa syytä', 'huonot valinnat', 'laiska'; when discussing lung cancer or COPD do not equate smoking with fault, note never-smokers also get them (check THL/Käypä hoito page when citing); for 'freedom and responsibility in lifestyles' present responsibility as shared among individual, community and policy (Health in All Policies) and explicitly include the critiques of victim blaming; people with disease are named as people with, not 'sufferers' or 'victims'; no weights, BMI cutoffs or calories (project rule).

VACCINES WITHOUT FALSE BALANCE: state the evidence and the official programme (link THL, read the THL vaccination programme and safety pages, since the safety page URLs tried returned 404; locate the current ones from thl.fi navigation); describe side effects with frequency category from THL, not omitted and not dramatised; explain how safety is monitored; explain herd immunity; treat hesitancy as a communication topic ('miksi tieto ei aina vakuuta', trust, misinformation literacy) not as a 'both sides' debate about whether vaccines work; do not give a debunk-quote that repeats a myth in a vivid form (use 'truth sandwich': fact, brief myth labelled, fact); do not shame the unvaccinated; personal medical decisions go to the student health nurse.

SCREENING AND GENE TECHNOLOGY: give the screening criteria (benefit, harm, false positives, overdiagnosis) as a neutral framework applied to a fictional case; prenatal screening: legal facts first, voluntary nature (verify in current THL guidance), the viewpoint of disability rights movements and of parents' autonomy both presented, no wording that treats a person with a condition as a 'burden'; gene technology: separate somatic therapy, research, testing and germline editing, give the legal status as read from a primary page (Finlex Geenitekniikkalaki, Laki lääketieteellisestä tutkimuksesta), no 'playing God' framing.

PRIORITISATION: teach with the Finnish framework (read the ETENE or STM page on prioritisation and the Health Care Act on hoidon tarve and kiireellisyys before citing); show the competing criteria (need, benefit, equality, cost-effectiveness) applied to a fictional case with no real patient and no age or disability ranking presented as correct; state that decisions are made by medical criteria and law, not by social worth.

SOURCES STILL TO READ BEFORE WRITING: Finlex ajantasa text of 239/1970, 785/1992, 1237/2006 hedelmöityshoitolaki, 1326/1990 / 2012/ geenitekniikkalaki; THL abortion statistics and legal page; THL vaccination programme and safety pages; ETENE statements and publications (esp. end-of-life 2011, prioritisation, patients' rights) with their Finnish pages; eduskunta page on the euthanasia initiative; WHO media guide PDF; Mieli youth peer-support page; Tieteen termipankki via direct search for 'seurausetiikka' etc.; Duodecim Terveyskirjasto on ethics; any Nuorten Exit or Nuorisotalo help only if its own page names young people.

HELP LINK RULE: before including any service, read its page for the age group; currently verified for youth: Sekasin 12-29. Mieli Kriisipuhelin is general (adult and youth) and must be labelled as such. Always add 112 for acute danger and opiskeluterveydenhuolto / school welfare for the student's own questions.
research.versus_expected: The brief's expectation (non-moralising, legal-facts-first, safe messaging, a help box, no false balance in vaccines) is confirmed in approach; its list of help services needs a correction, because only Sekasin is verified as a youth service and Mieli's crisis line is general. Verification of the Finlex legal details and the THL vaccine pages fell short, since the fetch returned only navigation or 404, so the rules are graded partly likely or unverified and name the pages to read next. The euthanasia 2021 working-group outcome and the ETENE role are verified.

research.summary: TE3 touches 38 of the 81 task rows in the brief-003 mapping (72 tasks; sub-parts split the rows to 81). Those rows are 880 of 1,680 points offered, which is an upper bound. The first number below is the module label; the second is my weighting. TE3-labelled rows are 380 p in the JSON (15 rows); the brief-003 critic moved A26-9 (30 p) to mixed, giving 350 p (21%), the figure in brief 010. My own weighting of the 23 mixed rows gives about 557 p, or 33%, TE3-touching [M]. The 38 rows and their weights are listed in findings. The weights are my judgement from each row's description. The JSON has no TE3 weights, and brief 008's TE2 re-map has none either. Exam coverage is almost all 'not TE1' (no existing topic carried it) and needs a TE3 re-map. Seven formats recur: ethical analysis scored by number of named viewpoints (4/7/10/13 of 15 content points, 5 p deducted if the material is unused); table builds; a 20-item true/false set; multiple choice with penalty; a drop-down cloze; diagram, chart and map reading; and short answers with character limits. YTL's 2024 and 2025 pages confirmed two of those rows each (spot checks below). The 2025 self-care task is a six-part, character-limited task, which the earlier mapping did not record.

After the critic's four corrections TE3-only is 350 p (21%), the figure in brief 010 and brief 008. My weighted TE3 share over the 38 rows is about 557 p (33%), judged. Area 1, explanation models of disease and public-health history (s1, s2, t1; rows S23-1, S24-3, A25-1 item on the 1972 public health act, S26-7 history of HiAP). Carry: the four models in chronological order (demonic, humoral, miasma, multi-causal), each with its view of cause and of treatment (2 p each per model); the five child-mortality measures in order with the reason each worked (neuvola, vaccination, antibiotics, hospital network, public health act of 1972); what HiAP is and when it arose. Formats: ordering plus table, ordering plus explanation, multiple-choice item. About 80 p [M].

Area 2, epidemiological and demographic transition (s2, s4, t1; rows A25-7, A26-2 items, A25-1 and S26-1.2 on epidemiology). Carry: the model's name (epidemiologinen siirtymä, demografinen siirtymä or transitio), five stages with mortality, birth rate and population per stage, and causes (nutrition, sanitation, vaccines, family planning, chronic disease, ageing, shrinking population). The 3-curve diagram format needs reading practice, with each curve named. About 60-70 p [M].

Area 3, non-communicable diseases and cancer (s4, t2; rows S23-6, S24-1, A25-1, S26-1, S26-2, A26-9, A23-6, A26-1). Area 4, infectious diseases (s4, t2; rows S24-2, A24-3, A26-2, S25-3, S25-4, S26-1.2-1.4, A24-9, A25-1 tuberculosis item, S25-2 travel). recommendations: Re-map against the 38 rows (880 p) listed in findings, using the weights as a starting point and the critic-corrected module labels (A26-9 mixed; A23-5 and A26-7 TE2). Treat the 15 TE3-only rows (350 p) as the full-coverage test, and the mixed rows by weight.

Give the ethical-analysis topics the most room. They carry about 160-180 p across six sessions. Teach the seven viewpoints (values, virtues, consequences, rights, duties, motives, norms) and the actors. Model answers must name at least four viewpoints, use the supplied material, and be split into content and information-processing halves. Cases: prioritisation, biobank, AI health text, abortion (with the legal facts and unsafe-abortion context), food choices, STI notification. Abortion and euthanasia stay non-moralising and safe-messaging compliant.

Make the epidemiological-transition topic a diagram task with five stages and three named curves, and a table of causes per stage (nutrition, sanitation, vaccines, family planning, chronic disease, ageing).

The disease topics should carry a fact table (cause, transmission, prevention) for Lyme/tick-borne, HIV and other STIs, influenza, malaria, salmonella and waterborne infection, plus cold against influenza, with exam tasks that build the table from given lists. Include type 1 against type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, COPD, stroke, rheumatic disease, tuberculosis and carcinogens as concepts. Include water contamination, hygiene and global shortage (A24-9) and bone health.

The inequality topic needs real figure-reading tasks: two charts by socioeconomic group, an age-standardised map, a table by sex/age/education. State that age is not an accepted explanation for a standardised regional map. Teach the arguments for narrowing gaps, HiAP history and application, and the five WHO action areas as a given frame.

Add 20-item true/false and name-the-concept sets, a +2/-1/0 multiple-choice set, a drop-down cloze, and an error-finding set with the 1000-character limit, plus the 600/1000-character itsehoito/omahoito task, so every exam format has a TE3 practice task.

proposal.title: TE3-specific safety rules for the style guide
proposal.detail:
R1 Law first: every ethics page (28, 29) opens each issue with a 'Mitä laki sanoo' block; each legal statement has a Finlex/STM/THL link with read date; statutory figures other than the verified 12-week rule (week 20/24 limits, ages) are linked, not typed, until a reviewer reads the current Finlex text.
R2 Positions symmetric: at least two positions per issue, each in the words its holders use, similar length and tone, analysed through the seven viewpoints; never assign a view to a religious or other group ('ihmisillä on erilaisia näkemyksiä').
R3 The page never concludes for the student; tasks say 'analysoi', not 'kumpi on oikeassa'; is and ought never share a sentence.
R4 No loaded terms (murha, tappaa lapsen, suunnittelijavauva, 'leikkiä Jumalaa', 'kuolemanapu' as euphemism); use the statutory or clinical term, defined once; 'raskaana oleva' where the law's group is wider.
R5 No personal disclosure: no 'mitä sinä tekisit', no personal positions graded; fictional third-person cases only; no real named private individuals or patient cases (assessment guidance excludes the student's own values and behaviour).
R6 Inclusive fertility text describes who may receive treatment only as the current law allows, without implying a normal family; abortion text never judges reasons.
R7 End of life (29): flag suicide_selfharm, content note, help box; no method, means, place, dose or tool; no suicide case stories; euthanasia debate anchored on the 2021 'no shared view' and dated initiative status; palliative care presented as care the county must provide (link the pending bill as pending).
R8 Disease pages (23, 24): 'riskitekijä' not 'syy'; structural, environmental and genetic factors beside lifestyle; state that people with no risk factors also fall ill; no 'oma syy', 'huonot valinnat'; 'ihminen, jolla on ...' not 'sairastaja/uhri'; no weights, BMI cutoffs or calories (exam BMI/obesity rows covered by concept, practice data fictional non-weight).
R9 Vaccines (24): evidence and the THL programme stated; side effects by THL frequency, neither omitted nor dramatised; herd immunity explained; hesitancy taught as communication and trust (truth sandwich, no vivid myth quotes); no shaming; own vaccination decisions go to the health nurse.
R10 No medical advice (23-26): self-care page teaches concepts and reliable sources, gives no dosing; for own symptoms, opiskeluterveydenhuolto, doctor or 112.
R11 Screening and gene technology (28): neutral criteria framework (benefit, harm, false positive, overdiagnosis) on a fictional case; disability-rights view and parental-autonomy view both presented; nobody described as a burden; somatic therapy, testing, research and germline editing kept distinct.
R12 Prioritisation (29): competing criteria (need, benefit, equality, cost-effectiveness) on a fictional case; no age or disability ranking shown as correct; decisions rest on medical criteria and law, not social worth.
R13 Figures: every changing figure is a dated link; chart tasks use invented data labelled as invented.
Checker tests (pass/fail): legal block with dated links present; two or more symmetric positions; no concluding sentence; no emotive vocabulary; no method content; help box on 29; no real person; every viewpoint defined with a neutral example; content notes on 23, 28, 29.
